supporting_observations.claim: PowerShell execution is recorded on WS-MLOPEZ-01 at 13:44:39 UTC, several minutes after the reported approximate time. It ran as HARBOR-DENTAL\omar.haddad with the command line invoking \\FILE-HD-01\IT\Deploy-Patches.ps1.

The recorded launch matches the documented patching practice: the environment identifies omar.haddad as the administrator who remotely runs this script, and says workstation patching is scheduled during business hours. The evidence also records an omar.haddad network logon from WS-OHADDAD-01 shortly before the PowerShell process.

The PowerShell process launched wusa.exe to install a Windows 11 update package, and the workstation made a proxy connection to download.windowsupdate.com using a Windows Update Agent user agent. These events are consistent with patch installation.
The available records do not show the contents or integrity of Deploy-Patches.ps1, so they do not establish whether the script itself contained only the expected patching actions.

known_telemetry_limitations: Process creation records capture the PowerShell command line but not the contents or hash of the invoked script.
No PowerShell script-block, transcription, or AMSI content is included in the supplied records.
The records show PowerShell starting at 13:44:39 UTC, not at approximately 13:40 UTC as reported; the evidence cannot establish the exact time the user saw a window.
The supplied logs contain activity during the review window, but do not establish that all relevant endpoint telemetry was collected.
claims_not_established: Whether the contents and integrity of Deploy-Patches.ps1 were legitimate at execution time.
Whether the reported window was the PowerShell process recorded at 13:44:39 UTC.
Whether the user saw a window, or whether the recorded process was visible interactively.
